The provision of The Motor Vehicles Act,
 1988 (`Act' for short) makes it clear that the award  must be just, which means that compensation  should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately  restore the claimant to the position prior to the  accident.
The object of awarding damages is to
make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong  done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable  and equitable manner.

The Court or tribunal shall  have to assess the damages objectively and exclude  from consideration any speculation or fancy, though  some conjecture with reference to the nature of  disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A  person is not only to be compensated for the  physical injury, but also for the loss which he  suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that  he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full  life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities  which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries,
 and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn  or could have earned. (See C. K. Subramonia Iyer  vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376, R. D.
 Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Ltd. - 1995 (1)
 SCC 551 and Baker vs. Willoughby - 1970 AC 467).
